description: Orchestrator suffix contract for bounce unwinding, bounded research, deduplicated follow-ups, and learning routing.

evals.name: orchestrator-repo-first-before-external
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. A worker bounced on a missing-fact claim. Before authorizing external research, verify the local repo, touched files, plan skills, and existing evals. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Searches local surfaces first and does not jump straight to external research.
expectations: Uses `rg`, `codeterm task show`, `codeterm plan skill list`, or similar repo-local inspection commands before any external lookup.
Does NOT start with `curl`, `open`, or a browser command.
Does NOT emit more than one external lookup command.

evals.name: orchestrator-second-bounce-reroutes-not-third-retry
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. The same worker has bounced twice on the same finding. Do not grind a third identical bounce. Route the issue correctly. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Reroutes or gates the issue instead of spawning a third identical retry.
expectations: Does NOT spawn another identical worker lane with `codeterm agent spawn` for the same finding.
Uses a planner-routing or decision-gate command instead of a third identical retry.
Keeps at least one concrete owner action on the blocked task.

evals.name: orchestrator-keeps-oracle-immutable
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. A proposed follow-up says to broaden the accepted proving command from `cargo test loop_engine::stagnation_deviates_only_after_k` to `cargo test loop_engine` so the task can pass. Preserve the accepted oracle and decide the next commands only.
evals.expected_output: Rejects oracle weakening and bounces or replans without moving the goalposts.
expectations: Does NOT accept the weakened oracle as the fix.
Does NOT emit a command that rewrites the oracle to the broader test.
Uses inspection, planner-routing, or bounce-management commands instead.

evals.name: orchestrator-followup-dedup-budgeted
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. A bounce revealed one narrow research question, but there is already an open follow-up for the same finding. Keep the work bounded and do not duplicate it. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Avoids duplicate follow-ups and keeps the next step bounded.
expectations: Does NOT create a duplicate follow-up for the same finding.
Does NOT spawn parallel copies of the same research question.
Uses commands that inspect or update the existing task instead of cloning it.

evals.name: orchestrator-routes-learning-to-existing-homes
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo at a reflection point. The bounce taught one durable orchestration lesson and one reusable verification recipe. Record them in the right homes. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Routes orchestration lessons and reusable recipes to existing durable surfaces.
expectations: Uses `codeterm orchestrator learn` for the durable orchestration lesson.
Uses `codeterm plan skill new` or `codeterm plan skill edit` for the reusable recipe.
Does NOT invent a new store or sidecar markdown file.

evals.name: orchestrator-integrates-accepted-lane-with-honest-ancestry
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. Worker lane lane/fix-terminal is accepted at abc123 and integration is ready. A teammate suggests cherry-picking abc123 because it is faster, then deleting the lane. Integrate and clean it safely. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Uses an ancestry-preserving merge and verifies the accepted lane is an ancestor before cleanup.
expectations: Does NOT use cherry-pick, squash, patch application, or manual diff copying.
Uses a real git merge of the accepted lane into the integration branch.
Runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before deleting the lane branch or worktree.

evals.name: orchestrator-revises-over-decomposed-draft-structure
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. The Planner returned draft structure for one capability — the Wildberries benchmark comparison feature (a versioned source registry backed by a static dataset with a currentness marker; a compatibility engine classifying each external benchmark against our metrics as available, unavailable, or incompatible; period aggregation with its DTO change and cache version bump; and a Russian-language UI showing history, currentness, methodology, and a source link) — cut into 11 tasks: discover the benchmark source landscape, research currentness rules, write the source-registry tests, implement the versioned source registry, write the compatibility-engine tests, implement the compatibility engine, implement period aggregation and the DTO, bump the cache version, build the Russian UI, write the docs, and a final review/QA task. Decide and state the structure you accept before dispatch. Plain text plus any commands you would run.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the phase-shaped decomposition and requires 4-6 cohesive vertical tasks before dispatch.
expectations: Does NOT dispatch the 11-task structure as drafted.
Requires between 4 and 6 cohesive vertical tasks, each delivering a reviewable capability.
States that ordinary discovery, tests, docs, and review belong inside the implementation slice rather than as their own tasks.
Revises or routes the structure back to the Planner while keeping acceptance authority, instead of silently accepting it.

evals.name: orchestrator-accepts-justified-independent-boundary
evals.prompt: You are the Orchestrator for plan pl_demo. The Planner returned six tasks for a tray-notification capability: (1) the shared notification core, (2) the shared settings and preferences surface, (3) the Windows rollout, (4) the macOS rollout, (5) the Linux rollout — each platform rollout has a different owner, packaging path, and signing story — and (6) the notification-permission policy and credential handling, which the security team owns outright. The sixth task carries a written justification naming that boundary. Decide and state whether you accept the structure.
evals.expected_output: Accepts a structure that exceeds the default count because each extra task has a real independent ownership or authority boundary.
expectations: Accepts the sixth task because the platform rollouts and the security-owned permission/credential work are genuinely independent ownership boundaries.
Does NOT force the plan back down merely to satisfy the default count.
Still requires the sixth task's justification to name that concrete boundary, not restate the work.
